subject: MATHEMATICS
purpose: Minimum readable physical size by SEMANTIC ROLE, not a single global floor. A global floor cannot express that a diagram label may legitimately be smaller than question body text while a solution body may not, and it was a global floor that allowed pages where text technically fit but was too small to teach from.
script_size_floor_note: Superscripts and subscripts are typeset at a reduced size; MathTypesetting refuses to render one below this floor rather than emitting an unreadable glyph.

MCQ_SELECTION.note: an option grid plus a choice box; a full lined page here is wasted area

PROOF.note: a proof needs room for GIVEN, licensed facts, derived statements and a conclusion

MULTIPART.note: a multipart item needs workspace per subpart, which is what overflowed in the Polynomials run

collision_policy.note: Two objects sharing a container are siblings and may not intersect. A child inside its container is legal containment, not a collision - which is why a page-bounds check alone could not see the Euclid two-up solution collision.

whitespace_policy.note: Large unused whitespace and microtype can coexist. If a learner-visible object is set below its preferred size while at least this share of the page is unused, the smaller type is a layout-policy choice rather than a page-capacity limit.

solution_packing_policy.note: One solution per page is correct when the content demands it. Two-up is an optimisation, not an invariant, and fixed-density packing is what produced the overlapping solution blocks.
